---
title: One UMAP per group
description: Fit a separate UMAP for every group with .over() or group_by().agg().
jupyter: python3
---

UMAP is fitted on all rows that an expression sees. In a window or group context, an expression
sees one group at a time, so you get an independent UMAP per group, all within a single query.

```{python}
#| echo: false
import numpy as np
import polars as pl
from sklearn.datasets import make_blobs

frames = []
for tenant in range(20):
    X, _ = make_blobs(n_samples=500, n_features=16, centers=4, random_state=tenant)
    frames.append(pl.DataFrame({"tenant": tenant, "embedding": X.astype(np.float32)}))
df = pl.concat(frames)
```

Say you have embeddings for 20 customers ("tenants") that should never be mixed:

```{python}
df.group_by("tenant").len().sort("tenant").head(3)
```

## With `.over()`

`.over()` keeps every row in place and adds the per-group embedding next to it:

```{python}
import polars_umap  # noqa: F401

out = df.with_columns(
    xy=pl.col("embedding").umap.fit_transform(random_state=0).over("tenant"),
)
out.head(3)
```

Each group gets exactly the result it would get on its own:

```{python}
one = df.filter(pl.col("tenant") == 7).select(
    pl.col("embedding").umap.fit_transform(random_state=0)
)
out.filter(pl.col("tenant") == 7)["xy"].equals(one["embedding"], check_names=False)
```

## With `group_by().agg()`

`group_by().agg()` gives one row per group, with lists of results. `explode()` turns them back into
rows:

```{python}
per_tenant = df.with_row_index("id").group_by("tenant", maintain_order=True).agg(
    "id", xy=pl.col("embedding").umap.fit_transform(random_state=0)
)
per_tenant.head(3)
```

```{python}
per_tenant.explode("id", "xy").head(3)
```

## Why this is fast

Polars runs the groups concurrently, and every UMAP shares one thread pool, so the machine is
used fully without oversubscribing it. In the [benchmarks](benchmarks.qmd), one `.over()` query
fitting 1,000 UMAPs took 18 seconds, against 58 seconds for a Python loop over polars-umap.

::: {.callout-tip}
## kNN indices are per group too

`.umap.knn().over("group")` returns neighbor indices relative to the start of each group, not the
whole frame. Add a row index per group (`pl.int_range(pl.len()).over("group")`) to join them back.
:::
